q: How tall is the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It leans about 4 degrees, down from 5.5 before engineers steadied it in 2001.

q: In what year did the Sydney Opera House open?
hint: For scale: the Beatles split up in 1970.
card: Its architect, Jørn Utzon, left the project in 1966 and never saw it finished.

q: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting every branch?
hint: For scale: the Earth is about {40,075 km} around the equator.
card: The figure comes from a 2012 Chinese survey that measured every wall, trench and branch.

q: How tall is the Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio, not counting its pedestal?
hint: For scale: a giraffe is about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Its outstretched arms span 28 metres, almost as wide as it is tall.

q: In what year was the Eiffel Tower completed?
hint: For scale: Thomas Edison demonstrated his light bulb in 1879.
card: It was built as the entrance arch for a World’s Fair and was meant to stand for only 20 years.

q: How long is the Channel Tunnel between England and France?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
card: About 38 km of it runs under the seabed, the longest undersea stretch of any tunnel.

q: How tall are the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world.

q: In what year did the Brooklyn Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the US Civil War ended in 1865.
card: Its main span was the longest suspension span in the world when it opened.

q: How tall is the Hoover Dam?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty, ground to torch, is about {93 m}.
card: Its concrete was cooled with chilled-water pipes; left alone it would have taken over a century to cool.

q: In what year did the Empire State Building open?
hint: For scale: the Wall Street Crash happened in 1929.
card: It went up in about 13 months, at times rising more than four floors a week.

q: How long is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, the world’s longest bridge?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
card: It carries the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed railway, much of it over rice paddies and lakes.

q: How many seconds does sunlight take to reach Earth?
hint: For scale: moonlight reaches us in about 1.3 seconds.
card: So you always see the Sun as it was a little over eight minutes ago.

q: What is the diameter of the Moon?
hint: For scale: the USA is about {4,500 km} wide.
card: The Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year.

q: Roughly how hot is the surface of Venus?
hint: For scale: lead melts at {327 °C}.
card: Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though it is nearly twice as far from the Sun.

q: In what year did Yuri Gagarin become the first person in space?
hint: For scale: the Korean War ended in 1953.
card: His flight, Vostok 1, lasted 108 minutes and circled Earth once.

q: How many Earth days long is a year on Mercury?
hint: For scale: an Earth month is about 30 days.
card: Yet one Mercury day, sunrise to sunrise, lasts about 176 Earth days.

q: What speed must something reach to escape Earth’s gravity from the surface?
hint: For scale: a rifle bullet flies at about {1 km/s}.
card: That is about 40,000 km/h. Staying in low orbit takes a little less, about 7.8 km/s.

q: In what year was Voyager 1 launched?
hint: For scale: the first Space Shuttle flew in 1981.
card: It is now the most distant human-made object, more than 20 billion km away.

q: How many hours long is a day on Jupiter?
hint: For scale: an Earth day is 24 hours.
card: It is the fastest-spinning planet, which visibly squashes it at the poles.

q: How many Earths would fit side by side across the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter is about 11 Earths across.
card: By volume, the Sun could hold about 1.3 million Earths.

q: What is the average distance from the Earth to the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter is about five times farther from the Sun than we are.
card: This distance is one astronomical unit, the yardstick of the solar system.

q: In what year was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet?
hint: For scale: the euro became cash in 2002.
card: The vote was taken at the International Astronomical Union’s meeting in Prague.

q: How many people have walked on the Moon?
hint: For scale: NASA flew nine crewed missions to the Moon.
card: All of them walked there between 1969 and 1972; no one has been back since.

q: How many legs does a lobster have?
hint: For scale: insects have six legs.
card: Lobsters taste and smell with tiny hairs on their legs.

q: Roughly how much does an adult male African elephant weigh?
hint: For scale: a family car weighs about {1,500 kg}.
card: Despite that bulk, elephants walk almost silently on padded feet.

q: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
hint: For scale: most spiders have eight.
card: The three small ones on top of its head sense light and help it hold a level flight.

q: How many chambers does a cow’s stomach have?
hint: For scale: a human stomach has just one.
card: The largest, the rumen, can hold well over 100 litres of chewed grass.

q: Up to how many times a minute can a hummingbird’s heart beat?
hint: For scale: a resting human heart beats about 70 times a minute.
card: At night some hummingbirds drop into torpor, slowing it to under 100.

q: For how many minutes can a sperm whale hold its breath on a dive?
hint: For scale: most people can manage about one minute.
card: They dive past 1,000 metres to hunt squid in total darkness.

q: How tall can an ostrich grow?
hint: For scale: a typical doorway is about {2 m} tall.
card: An ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain.

q: What is the widest wingspan of a wandering albatross?
hint: For scale: an average man is about {1.75 m} tall.
card: It can glide for hours without flapping, covering thousands of kilometres a week.

q: Roughly how many neurons are in the human brain?
hint: For scale: a honeybee’s brain has about a million.
card: They link up through something like 100 trillion connections.

q: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
hint: For scale: an adult cat has 30.
card: Puppies have 28 baby teeth and lose them by about six months old.

q: How fast can a peregrine falcon dive?
hint: For scale: a Formula 1 car tops out around {350 km/h}.
card: That makes it the fastest animal on Earth.

q: Roughly what percentage of an adult human body is water?
hint: For scale: about 71% of Earth’s surface is ocean.
card: The brain and heart are closer to three-quarters water.

q: In what year did the Great Fire of London happen?
hint: For scale: Shakespeare died in 1616.
card: It destroyed over 13,000 houses, yet only a handful of deaths were recorded.

q: In what year did American women win the right to vote nationwide?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: New Zealand had given women the vote back in 1893, the first self-governing country to do so.

q: In what year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
hint: For scale: Vikings first raided Lindisfarne in 793.
card: Its story is stitched into the Bayeux Tapestry, which is about 70 metres long.

q: In what year was Napoleon defeated at Waterloo?
hint: For scale: the French Revolution began in 1789.
card: The battlefield lies in today’s Belgium, about 15 km south of Brussels.

q: In what year did the Black Death reach Europe?
hint: For scale: Marco Polo set off for China in 1271.
card: It killed perhaps a third to a half of Europe’s population within a few years.

q: In what year did Martin Luther publish his Ninety-five Theses?
hint: For scale: the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453.
card: Printing presses spread his ideas across Germany within weeks.

q: In what year did the Chernobyl nuclear disaster happen?
hint: For scale: the Live Aid concerts were held in 1985.
card: The exclusion zone around it still covers about 2,600 square kilometres.

q: In what year did the Mayflower reach America?
hint: For scale: Shakespeare died in 1616.
card: About 100 passengers made the crossing, which took 66 days.

q: In what year was the Boston Tea Party?
hint: For scale: George Washington was born in 1732.
card: About 340 chests of tea were dumped into Boston Harbor.

q: In what year did India gain independence?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: Independence Day is celebrated every year on 15 August.

q: In what year was the first email sent between two computers?
hint: For scale: the first video game console went on sale in 1972.
card: Ray Tomlinson chose the @ sign to separate the user from the computer’s name.

q: In what year was the Statue of Liberty dedicated?
hint: For scale: Thomas Edison demonstrated his light bulb in 1879.
card: It was a gift from France; its copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick.

q: In what year did the first jet airliner enter passenger service?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: It was the de Havilland Comet, which cut flight times almost in half.

q: What is the wingspan of an Airbus A380?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737 spans about {36 m}.
card: Its wings cover about 845 square metres, roughly two basketball courts.

q: How many transistors are on Apple’s M1 chip?
hint: For scale: the first microprocessor, in 1971, had about 2,300.
card: Each one is just a few nanometres across, far smaller than a virus.

q: What is the rail speed record, set by a French TGV in 2007?
hint: For scale: a Formula 1 car tops out around {350 km/h}.
card: The record run used a specially shortened train with bigger wheels and boosted voltage.

q: How many engines powered the first stage of the Saturn V moon rocket?
hint: For scale: SpaceX’s Super Heavy booster has 33.
card: Together they burned more than 12 tonnes of propellant every second.

q: In what year was the first call made from a handheld mobile phone?
hint: For scale: the Watergate scandal broke in 1972.
card: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the call on a New York street, to a rival at Bell Labs.

q: How many seconds did the Wright brothers’ first powered flight last?
hint: For scale: it covered about {37 m}.
card: The whole flight was shorter than the wingspan of a Boeing 747.

q: How many pixels does a 4K Ultra HD screen have?
hint: For scale: a Full HD screen is 1,920 by 1,080 pixels.
card: The name comes from its width of roughly 4,000 pixels.

q: What top speed did the X-15 rocket plane reach, the fastest crewed aircraft?
hint: For scale: Concorde cruised at about {2,180 km/h}.
card: It flew so high that some of its pilots earned astronaut wings.

q: In what year did the Boeing 747 begin carrying passengers?
hint: For scale: Concorde first flew in 1969.
card: It more than doubled passenger capacity and earned the nickname Jumbo Jet.

q: In what year was a barcode first scanned at a store checkout?
hint: For scale: the first Apple computer went on sale in 1976.
card: The first item scanned was a pack of Wrigley’s chewing gum.

q: How many squares are on a chessboard?
hint: For scale: a tic-tac-toe grid has nine.
card: Counting squares of every size, there are actually 204.

q: What is the area of Australia?
hint: For scale: France is about 550,000 square km.
card: It is the only country that covers an entire continent.

q: Roughly how many languages are spoken in the world today?
hint: For scale: the European Union has 24 official languages.
card: About 40% of them are endangered, many with fewer than 1,000 speakers.

q: How deep is Lake Baikal, the world’s deepest lake?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: It holds roughly a fifth of the world’s unfrozen fresh surface water.

q: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world’s highest waterfall?
hint: For scale: Niagara Falls drops about {51 m}.
card: Much of the water turns to mist before it reaches the bottom.

q: Roughly how many islands make up Indonesia?
hint: For scale: the Philippines has more than 7,000.
card: Only about 6,000 of them are inhabited.

q: Roughly how large is the Sahara Desert?
hint: For scale: France is about 550,000 square km.
card: Sand dunes cover only about a quarter of it; most of it is rocky plateau.

q: How many dots are there on a standard six-sided die?
hint: For scale: opposite faces of a die always add up to seven.
card: That same rule means the 1, 2 and 3 faces always meet at one corner.

q: How tall is Mount Kilimanjaro?
hint: For scale: Mount Everest is {8,849 m} tall.
card: Despite sitting near the equator, its summit still has glaciers.

q: Roughly how many litres of air does an adult breathe in a day?
hint: For scale: one relaxed breath is about half a litre.
card: That is enough to fill about 50 bathtubs.

q: How many minutes are in a week?
hint: For scale: an hour has 60 minutes.
card: That is seven days of 1,440 minutes each.

q: How fast does sound travel through water?
hint: For scale: a jet airliner cruises at about {250 m/s}.
card: That is why whales can hear one another across huge distances.
